SMTO-UI-0032 — A message starting with / can't be queued

GUID: 4303bed8-f605-46f7-803a-4254815accfa
Slug: ui-command-not-queueable
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • Text that starts with a slash (/) is treated as an SMTO command, not a request for the Agent, so it can't wait in the queue. Your queue didn't change.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. To run an SMTO command, type it in the main message box and press Enter. Don't put it in a queued message. Commands typed in the message box run right away instead of waiting in the queue.
  2. If your request just happens to begin with a folder path or slash, add a word in front, for example "Open /home/notes.txt" instead of "/home/notes.txt". SMTO only treats text as a command when the slash comes first.
  3. If you were editing a message in the Queued list, change its first character so it doesn't start with /, then select Save. Saving an edited queued message checks the same rule as sending a new one.

What success looks like

  • Your command runs from the message box, or your reworded message appears in the Queued list.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, with the text you were trying to queue.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Prompt-queue validation rejected text whose first non-space character is "/", because slash text is reserved for application commands and is not queued as an Agent prompt.

What this means

  • The queued prompt begins with a slash after trimming. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • The queued prompt begins with a slash after trimming.

How to diagnose it

  • Confirm whether the intended input is a command or an ordinary Agent task.

How to fix it

  • prompt_queue.js checkText() throws ui_command_not_queueable when the trimmed prompt starts with "/" (on enqueue or when saving an edited queued prompt). Run slash commands directly from the composer, where they are executed by the slash-command handler, or reword the prompt so it does not start with "/".
  • Use the application command menu for this command, or queue an ordinary task prompt.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The command uses its supported menu, or ordinary task text is queued.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
